content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED to a single-verse exchange and cites the two father-references in Luke 2:48-49 as the reason, so it treats a two-meaning verse as open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.","room":"The phrase 'When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open' could mean (1) a two-meaning verse is settled and cannot be UNDERDETERMINED, or (2) it remains open between the meanings; I read K-S2 as (1).","why":"The judge labels the Luke 2:48-49 exchange UNDERDETERMINED while relying on the qualified 'thy father'/'my Father' wording, contrary to K-S2's rule that such two-meaning verse words both stand and are not open."}
